theory.intro: To solve an equation such as $\sin\theta=k$ for $0^{\circ}\le\theta<360^{\circ}$, find the acute reference angle from the positive value of $k$, then use the sign of $k$ (ASTC) to place $\theta$ in the correct two quadrants. Each quadrant gives one solution, so most equations have two.
facts: Enter the **positive** value of the ratio into the inverse function to get the acute reference angle $A$.

The sign of $k$ fixes the quadrants: $\sin\theta>0\Rightarrow$ Q1, Q2; $\sin\theta<0\Rightarrow$ Q3, Q4; $\cos\theta>0\Rightarrow$ Q1, Q4; $\cos\theta<0\Rightarrow$ Q2, Q3; $\tan\theta>0\Rightarrow$ Q1, Q3; $\tan\theta<0\Rightarrow$ Q2, Q4.
Each quadrant supplies one solution: $\theta=A$, $180^{\circ}-A$, $180^{\circ}+A$ or $360^{\circ}-A$.
Rearrange first: turn $a\,\text{trig}\,\theta+b=0$ into $\text{trig}\,\theta=\text{value}$ before finding $A$.
Boundary values ($\sin\theta=\pm1$, $\cos\theta=\pm1$, a ratio $=0$) sit on an axis and may give just one solution, or two on opposite sides.
steps: Find the acute reference angle using the positive value
Use the sign to choose the two quadrants

mastery.question_text: Solve $2\sin\theta-1=0$ for $0^{\circ}\le\theta<360^{\circ}$, and state which solution is obtuse.
mastery.solution_text:
$2\sin\theta-1=0$
$\sin\theta=\dfrac{1}{2}$
This is positive, so $\theta$ is in Q1 or Q2.
Reference angle: $A=30^{\circ}$.
Q1: $\theta=30^{\circ}$
Q2: $\theta=180^{\circ}-30^{\circ}=150^{\circ}$
$\theta=30^{\circ},150^{\circ}$; the obtuse solution is $150^{\circ}$.

$2\cos\theta+2=0$
$\cos\theta=-1$
$\cos\theta=-1$ only at the left of the unit circle, so there is a single solution.
$\theta=180^{\circ}$

$2\cos\theta-\sqrt{2}=0$
$\cos\theta=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
This is positive, so $\theta$ is in Q1 or Q4.
Reference angle: $A=45^{\circ}$.
Q1: $\theta=45^{\circ}$
Q4: $\theta=360^{\circ}-45^{\circ}=315^{\circ}$
$\theta=45^{\circ},315^{\circ}$
